Oblivion ESM/ESP binary format confirmed: 20-byte record header (NOT the 16-byte header used by Skyrim/Fallout). Record = tag(4) + dataSize(4) + flags(4) + formID(4) + version(2) + unknown(2) = 20 bytes. GRUP = 'GRUP'(4) + size(4) + label(4) + groupType(4) + skip(4) = 20 bytes. Subrecord = tag(4) + size(2) = 6 bytes, with size masked by (size & 0xFFFF). TES4 header record sits at offset 0 with dataSize=744, flags=1, formID=0, so the first GRUP is at offset 764 (20 + 744). app/src/main/cpp/assets/esm_reader.cpp already implements this format correctly (L116 'TES4 record: 20-byte header', L183 'remaining 16 bytes', L86 'GRUP header (20 bytes)', L471 size & 0xFFFF + offset += 6). CRITICAL: records with size 0 are LEGAL and are NOT terminators; treating them as errors truncates the scan.

Oblivion Script VM instruction format (confirmed from script_vm.cpp and script_disasm.cpp): each instruction is opcode(uint16 LE) + argLength(uint16 LE) + argData(argLength), i.e. a 4-byte header. argLength==0 instructions (ADD/POP/NEG/CMP) still consume 4 bytes. STOP must be 0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00. Opcode values: STOP=0x0000, ADD=0x0001, NEG=0x0006, JUMP=0x0010, JUMP_Z=0x0011, PUSH_INT=0x0012, PUSH_FLOAT=0x0013, PUSH_REF=0x0015, POP=0x0016, DUP=0x0017, GET_LOCAL=0x0020, GET_GLOBAL=0x0022, CALL=0x1000. JUMP/JUMP_Z targets are ABSOLUTE program counters (ctx.setPC(target)), not relative offsets. execute(ctx, maxInstructions) returns VMResult::FrameBudget when the budget is exhausted.

app/src/main/cpp/include/glm/glm.hpp is a hand-written minimal GLM stub, NOT real GLM. vec3 exposes only vec3(), vec3(x,y,z), public x/y/z, operator+ - * /, dot, cross, length, normalize. There is NO operator[] and NO single-float constructor, so 'v[i]' and 'glm::vec3(0.0f)' fail to compile. Use explicit component math or copy into a float array, and always pass three floats to the constructor. Free functions glm::dot / glm::cross / glm::length / glm::normalize do exist.

QuestManager semantics (deliberate, do not 'fix'): updateObjectiveProgress() auto-completes a quest as soon as allObjectivesCompleted() is true, by calling checkAndCompleteQuest() -> completeQuest(). completeQuest() is NOT idempotent - it returns false and logs a warning if the quest is already COMPLETED (failQuest() is symmetric). Auto-completion is called from both updateObjectiveProgress() and update(). QuestStageManager::checkCompletionStage() forwards completeQuest()'s bool, but its only call site (quest_stage_manager.cpp:350) discards it, so the non-idempotent result causes no production harm.

CharacterStatus::initialize(baseHealth, baseMana, level) no longer applies level scaling; it sets maxHealth = baseHealth, maxMana = baseMana, and now also stores this->level = level. CollisionWorld::getBodyCount() now returns the new liveBodyCount_ member instead of bodies.size(). bodies is a slot array: addBody() reuses freeSlots or push_backs, and removeBody() only sets id=-1, isActive=false and push_backs the slot, so the vector never shrinks. removeBody() also gained a double-free guard (if bodies[bodyId].id == NULL_BODY return;). getBodyCount() has no production consumers - only Phase30 tests - so the capacity->live-count change is behaviour-neutral outside tests.

Consequently maxMagicka is NEVER persisted. Changing only L686 to maxMagicka would mix two attributes into one stat, so decide first whether Player gets a real magicka pool. Deferred to Phase69 (persistence).

Oblivion MGEF/SPEL/ENCH/INGR/ALCH binary layout (empirically confirmed with Python probes mgef_probe7..12 against the real Oblivion.esm). MGEF subrecord is DATA (36 or 64 bytes; NOT MEDT): off4=baseCost(float), off8=actorValue(uint32), off12=school(0-5), off16=flags. SPEL subrecord SPIT is 16 bytes: off0=spellType, off4=cost, off8=level, off12=uninitialized (0xCDCDCD00; NOT flags). EFID (4 bytes) is the MGEF editorID ASCII code (e.g. FIDG, RESP, INVI), NOT a formID. EFIT is 24 bytes: off0-3 = EFID echo, off4=magnitude, off8=area, off12=duration, off16=unused, off20=actorValue. The old code read magnitude/area/duration from off0/off4/off8, i.e. 4 bytes off; that was the direct cause of 0 spells being assigned. INGR/ALCH: DATA is only 4 bytes (float weight) and ENIT is 8 bytes (off0=value, off4=flags).

Oblivion EFIT magnitude is stored as EITHER int32 OR float depending on the record (proven by mgef_probe11: int values appear as denormal floats such as 1.4e-45). Read it with the helper readFloatOrInt() in assets/esm_reader.cpp: if the float is 0, non-finite, |f|<1e-6, or |f|>1e9, reinterpret the 4 bytes as int32. Distribution of raw off4 values across 1137 SPEL EFITs: 0(334), 100(226), 10(214), 20(169), 5(136), 50(119), 30(87), 15(84), 25(82), 1(41).

Oblivion MGEF actorValue (DATA off8) full semantics, confirmed for all 145 MGEFs (mgef_probe12). 0 = special/generic effect (LOCK, OPEN, DISPL, TELE, REAN, TURN, VAMP, DIAR, DIWE, DRSK, SUDG, POSN, COCR, COHU, LGHT, ABAT, ABSK, CUxx, FOAT, FOSK, REAT, STRP, SEFF). 8 = Health (ABHE, DGHE, DRHE, FIDG, FOHE, FRDG, REHE, SHDG). 9 = Magicka (ABSP, DGSP, DRSP, FOSP, RESP; 'SP' = spell points = Magicka, so Restore Magicka is RESP, not RSPA). 10 = Fatigue (ABFA, DGFA, DRFA, FOFA, REFA). 11 = Speed (BRDN, FTHR). 33-70 = skills/attributes (CALM=33, DEMO=34, FOMM=40, NEYE=41, SHLD=43, CHML=46, INVI=47, PARA=48, SLNC=49, SABS=52, RFLC=53, WABR=55, WAWA=56, STMA=57, DTCT=58, REDG=59, TELE=60, FISH/RSFI/WKFI=61, FRSH/RSFR/WKFR=62, RSDI/WKDI=63, RSMA/WKMA=64, RSNW/WKNW=65, RSPA=66, RSPO/WKPO=67, LISH/RSSH/WKSH=68, DARK=70). >100 = formID link; ALL 62 Conjuration MGEFs are formID links (Bound Weapons BW01-BW08, Summons Z001-Z019, Bound Armor BABO-BASH, MYTH/MYHL). Use a threshold of 200 to split actorValue from linkedFormID.

Oblivion SPEL records do NOT store a magic school; it must be derived from the spell's magic effects. Because EFID holds an editorID code rather than a formID, references cannot be resolved during the single decode pass. Implemented a two-phase scheme: ESMFile::resolveMagicReferences() runs after all records are decoded and maps effectCodes -> effectFormIDs and derives spell.school from the first effect's MGEF school. ESMManager::rebuildIndices() runs a SECOND pass that builds a global editorID->MGEF map across all loaded files and re-resolves each file, so DLC plugin spells link to master (Oblivion.esm) MGEFs. MagicEffectData pointers in ESMManager::m_magicEffectByEditorID are only valid after rebuildIndices() (it clears them on every rebuild).

game/spell_manager.cpp mgefToEffectType() now takes const oblivion::MagicEffectData* instead of a formID. The old hardcoded formID switch (0x0001E825 etc.) was entirely wrong: real MGEF formIDs are 0x00001881-style, so every effect fell back to DAMAGE. Classification now keys off the MGEF editorID code plus school/linkedFormID: FIDG/FRDG/SHDG/DG*/DR*/WK*/AB* -> DAMAGE, REHE/FOHE/CU* -> HEAL, RESP/FOSP/FOMM -> RESTORE_MANA, REFA/FOFA -> RESTORE_STAMINA, PARA -> PARALYZE, INVI -> INVISIBILITY, school==1 && linkedFormID!=0 -> SUMMON, fallback = DAMAGE when school==2 else FORTIFY_ATTR.

Confirmed ESM subrecord layouts for the secondary record types. PGRD: PGRP is a 16-byte stride (x,y,z float + unused uint32), PGAG is 1 bit per point (bytes = ceil(N/8)), PGRR is 4-byte stride, PGRL is 12 raw bytes; PGRD has no own cell formID, it must use the GRUP parent cell formID. PGRD is always a compressed record (flags bit18) and the reader decompresses it before decoding. GMST: EDID + DATA whose type is derived from the first EDID character (s=string, f=float, i=int, b=bool). GLOB: EDID + FNAM(1, type char) + FLTV(4, float). LTEX: EDID + ICON + HNAM(3, rgb) + SNAM(1). DOOR: EDID + FULL + MODL + MODB(4) + SCRI(4) + SNAM(4) + ANAM(4) + FNAM(1 flags). GRAS: EDID + MODL + MODB(4) + DATA(32) where DATA offset 2 is maxSlope. FURN: EDID + FULL + MODL + MODB(4) + MNAM(4). AMMO: EDID + FULL + MODL + MODB(4) + ICON + ENAM(4) + DATA(18). SLGM: EDID + FULL + MODL + MODB(4) + ICON + SCRI(4) + DATA(8) + SOUL(1, current soul) + SLCP(1, capacity). KEYM: EDID + FULL + MODL + MODB(4) + ICON + DATA(8). SBSP: EDID + DNAM(12, 3 floats). SGST: EDID + FULL + MODL + MODB(4) + MODT(96) + ICON + repeated EFID(4)+EFIT(24) + DATA(9). WTHR: EDID + CNAM + DNAM + NAM0(160) + FNAM(16) + HNAM(56) + DATA(15) + SNAM(8)*N. IDLE: EDID + MODL + MODB(4) + CTDA(24)*N + ANAM(1) + DATA(8). CSTY: EDID + CSTD(124) whose first 2 bytes are a uint16 (weaponFlags) followed by floats. LSCR: EDID + ICON + DESC + LNAM(12) whose first 4 bytes are a formID. ANIO: EDID + MODL + MODB(4) + DATA(4, formID). WATR: EDID + TNAM + ANAM(1) + FNAM(1) + MNAM(1) + SNAM(4) + DATA(102, floats) + GNAM(12). EFSH: EDID + ICON(1) + ICO2 + DATA(224) whose first int32s are flag groups.

ESM pitfall: LAND, PGRD, REFR, ACHR and ACRE records do not carry their own cell formID. The owning cell must be recovered by tracking the label of the enclosing GRUP with groupType == 6 (CellChildren). Two code paths need this: the file parse path uses a groupInfoStack and the memory parse path uses m_currentCellFormID. Oblivion GRUP types: 0=TopLevel, 1=WorldChildren, 2=InteriorCellBlock, 3=InteriorCellSubBlock, 4=ExteriorCellBlock, 5=ExteriorCellSubBlock, 6=CellChildren, 7=TopicChildren, 8=CellPersistentChildren, 9=CellTemporaryChildren. Also note SubRecord has no empty() member; use size() > 0.

ROOT CAUSE of the gameplay frame-rate ceiling, confirmed by measurement: ui/ui_draw_helper.cpp called glGetUniformLocation on EVERY draw call (2 per drawColoredQuad, 3 per drawTexturedQuad, 5 per drawGradientQuad, 7 per drawRadialGlow, 16 per draw3DTextureQuad). Each call is a synchronous round-trip to the GL server, so the in-game HUD issued hundreds per frame. Evidence chain: PerformanceMonitor reported a Min Frame Time floor of 37.19 ms (27 fps best case); pointing the camera at empty sky did not change the frame rate (so it was not fragment load); the title screen ran at 60 fps because it draws no HUD; simpleperf attributed 83.22% of samples to goldfish_pipe.ko:goldfish_pipe_read_write with under 0.1% in app code; top -H showed the GL thread at 96.5% and every other thread at 0.0%. FIX: memoize locations per (program, name) in an unordered_map keyed by program id, cleared in UIDrawHelper::cleanup(). RESULT: in-game 19.3 -> 42.7 fps, Average Frame Time 57.78 -> 22.06 ms, Min Frame Time 37.19 -> 15.63 ms, title unchanged at 60. Re-verified after the ndkVersion pin on a freshly restarted emulator: gameplay average 46.83 fps (window average 42.49, max 50.00), Current FPS 46.1, Min Frame Time 15.14 ms, Max Frame Time 27.20 ms, title 60-61 fps. engine/shader.cpp and ui/text_renderer.cpp already cached their locations, which is why the 3D mesh paths were never the bottleneck. LESSON: on this emulator any GL call that needs a server round-trip inside a per-frame loop is a frame-rate cliff - cache every location and never query GL state per draw. Remaining uncached call sites are low priority: ui/title_screen.cpp (3 per frame, but the title screen is already at 60 fps), renderer.cpp renderPlaceholderEntities() (debug path), geometry/cube.cpp, world/distant_lod/distant_lod_horizon.cpp.

TerrainData reworked to cut native heap and to fix a silent terrain bug. New layout: std::vector<int8_t> heightDeltas (1089 raw VHGT bytes) + float heightOffset + baseTextures[4] + textureFormIDs, with expandHeights()/heightAt() helpers and GRID = 33. Consumers updated: engine/renderer.cpp, world/landscape_renderer.cpp (expands once locally and reuses for 4 quadrants), assets/world_data_loader.cpp. Measured: native heap allocation 704,684 KB -> 430,916 KB; Native Heap SwapPss 629,158 -> 33,981 KB (-95%); TOTAL SWAP PSS 648,001 -> 49,735 KB (-92%). THE BUG THIS FIXED: the old decoder required the Morrowind 65x65 int16 VHGT (size() >= 8451) while TES4's VHGT is 1096 bytes, so hasHeights() was ALWAYS false and every terrain silently rendered as a flat plane. Expansion formula validated independently in Python against Oblivion.esm: (heightOffset + columnOffset + rowOffset) * 8.0f, 14,052/14,613 east-edge and 14,066/14,608 north-edge heights agree (96%; the rest are cells from different worldspaces sharing grid coords). VNML/VCLR parsing was deleted - calculateNormals() derives normals from heights and VCLR was unused.

Known remaining memory item, NOT yet fixed. engine/renderer.cpp assigns cell->heightData = terrain.expandHeights() inside the loop over all 31,823 terrain records, so all 14,686 matched exterior cells each hold 1089 floats (4356 B) = about 64 MB, although only the 9 active cells are ever rendered. Deliberately left alone because Cell::getTerrainHeightAt() reads heightData from other systems and returning 0 for an unloaded cell would change object placement and player grounding. Fixing it needs a compact or lazily expanded representation plus an audit of those callers. Note the current behaviour is MORE correct than before: the flat-terrain fallback meant only the 9 loaded cells had heights at all. plan.md previously claimed '9 active cells only, about 39 KB', which never matched the implementation and has been corrected.

Oblivion .fnt files carry NO vertical metrics (header bytes 76..344 are all zero), and f[1] is NOT an advance. Glyph boxes are tight ink bboxes plus ~1px padding, so advance = width and bearing_x = 0. Vertical metrics are measured at runtime from the atlas: capBaseline = mode of the ink-bottom row of ASCII 'A'-'Z', and per glyph baseline_rel = min(inkBottom, capBaseline). For kingthings_regular (fontSize 28, 512x512 atlas) capBaseline = 24. Glyph records are indexed by ASCII - 1.

text_renderer.cpp: when scanning a glyph box for its ink bottom you must walk EVERY row and keep the last row that has ink. Writing the loop as 'for (y = 0; y < h && last < 0; y++)' stops at the FIRST inked row and records the ink TOP, which made capBaseline collapse to 1 and pushed the whole menu row ~63px too high.

TitleScreen must apply its plain font style ONCE (applyPlainFontStyle in render(), guarded by fontStyleApplied) and restore it when leaving the title (releasePlainFontStyle on gameStarted/quitRequested). Saving/restoring setFontAlphaCurveEnabled/setFontOutlineEnabled/setFontSizeMultiplier every frame emitted 6 INFO lines per frame and made computeMenuLayout see a different fontSizeMultiplier_ than the draw call.

TextRenderer::getTextWidth()/getTextCapHeight() fold fontSizeMultiplier_ into their result, so a layout computed at one moment and drawn at another disagree. TitleScreen::computeMenuLayout() and rebuildMenuLayout() therefore divide the measured width/cap height by the current getFontSizeMultiplier() to normalise to multiplier 1.0, which is what the title screen draws with.

Adaptive launcher icon layout rules applied to Oblivion (2026). The 108dp adaptive canvas only guarantees the inner 66dp DIAMETER circle stays visible, i.e. a radius of 33/108 = 30.56% of the canvas - not 61.1% of the canvas, which is the diameter and is easy to confuse with the radius. scripts/generate_launcher_icons.py therefore fits the foreground and monochrome layers by their minimum enclosing circle at 61% of the canvas diameter, giving a measured maximum radius of 29.9-30.0%, and check_safe_zone() fails the build if any masked layer exceeds 30.56%. The background layer cannot be transparent by spec; Oblivion uses #1A1A1A via drawable/ic_launcher_background.xml with the natural bronze symbol as the foreground, plus ic_launcher_monochrome.png (white silhouette) for themed icons. Legacy API<26 icons bake the background in because no mask is applied there. Do not apply colour-key thresholding to the symbol alpha - the source alpha is already exact and thresholding destroys the dark parts of the artwork.

scripts/generate_launcher_icons.py is the single source of truth for all 24 launcher icon PNGs (mipmap-{ldpi..xxxhdpi}/ic_launcher{,_round,_foreground,_monochrome}.png). It renders them from app/src/main/assets/textures/ui/loading_symbol.png (512x512, opaque bounds 310x432) with 4x supersampling, and writes scripts/launcher_icon_manifest.json holding the sha256 of every generated PNG. That texture is a gitignored Bethesda asset, so a fresh clone and CI do not have it: --check therefore always verifies the committed manifest, and additionally compares decoded pixels only when the texture is present. The minimum enclosing circle is computed with a pure-numpy convex hull plus Welzl's algorithm so the only CI dependencies are pillow and numpy. .github/workflows/android.yml runs 'python3 scripts/generate_launcher_icons.py --check' right after Checkout, which is what stops Android Studio's template from silently replacing the icons with the default green robot again.

Oblivion Android title menu: MENU_OUTLINE_WIDTH is nearly exhausted as a thinning lever. text_renderer.cpp drawOblivionText stamps the outline 9 times; the 4 diagonal stamps reach ring*sqrt(2), so added ink scales with (0.5 + ring*sqrt(2)), not with ring. AsyncTaskManager had a real completion-ordering race, fixed on master as 47e691f4 (2026-09-25, session 964d16fb). Root cause: submit() wrapped each callable in a std::packaged_task, and packaged_task satisfies the caller's future from INSIDE the callable, so a caller woken by the future could read getStats() before workerThread() had run recordCompletion() and observe totalCompleted one short. That is what made Phase45UnitTests/Async_Statistics intermittently fail (39/40) and what the wiring agent reported as an app-side flake. Measured with a standalone probe before the fix: 27 of 500 iterations failed polling with wait_for(0ms), 2 of 4000 failed with wait() (the path the unit test uses). Fix: submit() now hands the task a std::function + std::promise and the task records completion BEFORE it publishes its result, so a ready future implies a counted completion. Secondary defect fixed by the same change: packaged_task stores a throwing task's exception in its shared state instead of rethrowing it, so workerThread()'s catch blocks never observed task failures and totalFailed_ stayed at 0 forever. The task now catches its own exception, counts the failure and forwards it to the promise (future::get() rethrows, getStats().totalFailed is real). avgExecutionTimeMs is now divided by every executed task, not only successful ones. After the fix: 20000 iterations of each probe mode fail zero times, a 200-iteration outcome probe (value, void, std and non-std exceptions) fails zero times.

SCDA 0x001C is a reference selector, not a source-line marker: [u16 0x001C][u16 refIndex], 4 bytes fixed, no payload. refIndex is a 1-based index into the reference list the compiler emitted for the command that follows. Proven over 1,373 of 1,373 records carrying the marker: max value never exceeds the record's distinct source reference count (median ratio 0.92, maximum 16, 795 records at 1 or below). The MQ13/MQ14 record settles it: the same actors get the same indices in two groups written in different orders (Burd 3, Ulrich 4, Viera 5, Martin 6, Jauffre 7, Baurus 8, Steffan 9; second group order 7,6,8,9,5,4,3). A VM must consume the 4 bytes and assign the calling reference; discarding the value breaks every bare Ref.command. The marker shares its numbering with the 0x72 reference operand, so the two ways of naming a reference agree inside one record: in corpus record 2395 the refs SE45zBossREF and SE45mBossREF alternate enable and disable as markers 1 and 2, and the three SetQuestObject calls that follow carry r 01 00, r 02 00 and r 01 00 in their payloads for those same two actors. Open question: a handful of long records appear to hand one actor two different indices, and every one of them is a record whose SCTX statements run together on merged lines; a decoder that holds the real record can settle it by comparing the index against the record's own reference list.

SCDA command-layer grammar is settled and carries no terminator byte: [u16 opcode][u16 argLength][argLength bytes]. argLength == 0 means no parameter block at all (3,763 of the 18,142 ordinary commands); argLength == 2 with payload [u16 0] is an explicit zero-argument block (all 8 0x10A5 RemoveMe, the 3 0x10DE CloseOblivionGate in record 2504, the 3 0x1165 ForceCloseOblivionGate); argLength above 2 is [u16 n][n typed tokens], where n is the argument count (0x110D SetQuestObject = 02 00 72 02 00 6e 00 00 00 00, 0x109E MoveTo = 01 00 72 0b 00). The tokenizer needs backtracking for the string family: a greedy left-to-right pass matches 13,180 of 14,379 payloads (91.66%) against 13,601 (94.59%) with backtracking, and the residual 778 are 0x1059 Message and 0x1000 MessageBox, whose argLength includes the padded body. Never mix the command layer (op >= 0x1000) with the anchor layer in one payload statistic: the structural anchors and 0x001C / 0x001D carry raw source text or nested streams, and treating a small opcode as length-bearing is what produced the invalid 117-unnamed / 78.61% census.

Oblivion QUST DATA subrecord is TWO independent bytes, not a single u16 bitfield: byte 0 = flags (only 7 distinct values {0,1,4,5,8,9,13}, a sparse bitfield over bits 0/2/3) and byte 1 = quest priority (31 distinct values in 0..100, dominated by 60 x140 / 50 x63 / 40 x38). All 390 QUST DATA subrecords are exactly 2 bytes. A reader that does uint16_t flags folds priority into the flag word and corrupts it. Also re-confirmed: CNAM is per stage block (all 2338 immediately preceded by a QSDT, zero unattributed), so a single per-stage logText cannot represent real data; SCHR is 1:1 with QSDT (2978 each) while SCDA is not, so any block index must be the QSDT ordinal, never the SCDA ordinal.

SCDA 43-record anchor imbalance ROOT CAUSE = malformed retail scripts, NOT a decoder fault. Replaying every record as a block machine from the byte stream alone (no SCTX): all 2646 records finish at depth 0, 0 records with else/elseif at depth 0, and exactly 43 records close a block that was never opened. Oblivion SCDA facts confirmed 2026-09-25: (1) 'else if X' is legal source and compiles to 0x0018 elseif, NOT else+if - the corpus has 7 'else if' lines yet else is 968 source against 968 opcodes exactly, so the two-word form emits no 0x0017. Oblivion INFO record topic ownership (measured 2026-09-25 over 19,278 INFO and 3,817 DIAL records). The OWNING topic is structural, not a subrecord: every INFO sits inside exactly one GRUP of type 7 whose 4-byte label equals the FormID of the DIAL record immediately preceding it (3,053/3,053 groups, label never 0). 2,961 distinct owning topics, dominated by conversation-framework entries: GREETING 3743, HELLO 1893, Rumors 1854, GOODBYE 1144, Attack 302, Question 205, Hit 105, Idle 86. GREETING alone holds 19.4% of all INFO. INFO.NAME is a SECOND DIAL reference carried by only 1,044 of 19,278 records; it can repeat (1 entry 837, 2:153, 3:38, 4:4, 5:6, 6:4, 7:1, 8:1 = 1,342 occurrences over 582 distinct DIAL targets); it sits at subrecord index 2 (right after DATA and QSTI, BEFORE TRDT, not at the end of the record); and it names a different topic than the owning group in 1,043 of 1,044 cases. For the twelve most-named topics, NOT ONE INFO both sits in that topic's own group and names it (Doubles 36/42/both 0, Join the Mages Guild 14/34/0, Mirili's Research 6/20/0, Umbacano 15/15/0, Savage Garden 2/13/0), and framework topics carry NAME zero times across their 8,936 records. NAME is additive, never an override. TCLT is a third DIAL reference (9,698 occurrences, 1,955 distinct, 100% resolving to DIAL and 0% to INFO) naming conversation-flow targets: GOODBYE 1081, TRANSITION 830, NeutralReceive 766, Rumors 472, SE 377, Question 363. Oblivion INFO carries NO TPIC and NO PNAM (Skyrim-shaped readers find nothing). Consequence: decodeInfo() must take the owning topic from the enclosing group label, treat NAME/TCLT as extra links, and never assume NAME is the owner. Recorded in plan.md.

Oblivion INFO.QSTI is the total, unambiguous quest link and reference resolution in the ESM must always be TWO-PASS. QSTI is present exactly once in all 19,278 INFO records (none has zero or two); its 337 distinct values ALL resolve to a QUST (337/337, zero unresolved) and reach 337 of the 390 quests, so registerQuests() can join dialogue to quests through QSTI alone. A single-pass resolver that compares QSTI against a QUST set it is still filling reports 337 FALSE unresolved values, because QUST records are not guaranteed to precede the INFO records that name them. Always build the complete FormID-to-tag map in pass 1, then resolve in pass 2. Also confirmed in the same measurement: GRUP type 7 immediately follows its DIAL record (3,053/3,053); GRUP type 0 label is the ASCII tag name (0x4C414944 = 'DIAL') and must never be read as a FormID; Oblivion DIAL FormIDs live in the low integer range (0x000000AA..0x0018D923) so small labels like 200 (0xC8 GREETING) and 210 (0xD2 HELLO) are real FormIDs.
